body:
Timely one - you have vignettes/introduction.Rmd open right now and this is in the section you rewrote.

introduction.Rmd:87 asserts

  identical(effect$total, effect$coherent + effect$configuration)

That is exact bit equality, and the identity is not exact in floating point. Measured on ordinary data - 8 features, 3 conditions, 3 runs, searchlights(2.01), seed 53:

  max abs (total - (coherent + configuration))   1.387779e-17
  all(diff == 0)                                 FALSE
  all.equal at 1e-12                             TRUE

Two test assertions do the same thing at tolerance = 0: test-workflow.R:35-36 and test-views.R:44-45.

The mathematics is fine and the prose claim should stay - configuration IS derived as total minus coherent, and that is what stops drift across reruns. But coherent + fl(total - coherent) does not always round-trip to total; it does when no rounding occurs, which depends on the magnitudes. Your fixtures happen to land there.

Why it matters more for the vignette line than the tests: line 87 is a check a READER can run on their own data. When rounding bites they get FALSE from a check the vignette presents as verifying an exact additive split, and they will read that as the decomposition being broken rather than as floating point.

Suggested: 1e-12 in all three places. It is already used elsewhere in the same test files and passes here with several orders of spare room.

Unrelated but worth knowing since you are in these files: I regression-checked seven invariants I had previously verified against your working tree just now, and all seven still hold - the conservation law across frames, metric K=I recovering the additive frame, query-first equalling materialized, geometry_spectrum still refusing a plan, reverse_bridge still an involution, and the beta-path accessors still refusing with the capability message you added. Nothing you have changed has broken anything I had verified. The only two apparent failures in my run were my own test construction, and this exact-equality issue is the one real thing that fell out of it.

Also noticed: introduction.Rmd:112 now carries d_ij = c^T G c = G_ii + G_jj - 2G_ij. That is bd-01KZY96KKH0X14EC62S2VX2RV9 - connecting geometry to the second-moment matrix G - and it was the highest payoff-per-effort item in my whole review. Good to see it land.
